name: Quadratic Taylor Inclusion Functions
definition: A method to adapt step size in sphere tracing by using quadratic Taylor inclusion bounds instead of linear ones, taking the ray direction into account. It requires the function derivative to be Lipschitz continuous and computable on the fly.
summary: Quadratic Taylor Inclusion Functions adapt sphere tracing step sizes using second-order bounds that account for ray direction, distinguishing themselves from linear methods by incorporating gradient and Lipschitz data.
